source.title: A Dimension-Two Counterexample to the Separable Jacobian Conjecture in Characteristic Two
source.author: Mondello, Romy
source.theorem: Theorem 1.2 in the numbering of the request; the source labels it \label{thm:main} and it is the only theorem environment in main.tex

map.note: Every printed coefficient is 1. Monomials are given as [i, j] meaning x^i*y^j, with the coefficient in F_2.
map.linear_part_note: read off the printed P and Q: the degree-1 part of P is x and of Q is y; the paper independently states JF(0,0) = I_2

collision.paper_remark_verbatim: They are distinct as \(k\)-points, so \(F\) is not injective on points.

theorem_claims_verbatim: the function-field extension is separable, and, over an algebraic closure \(\Omega\) of \(k(P,Q)\), the geometric generic fiber has exactly three \(\Omega\)-valued points;
\[ F(0,1)=F(1,0)=F(1,1)=(0,1), \] so \(F\) is not an automorphism.
ambiguity_notes: No entry required a judgement call. Every monomial, exponent and coefficient is printed explicitly in the displayed equations of the theorem; all coefficients are 1; there are no ellipses, no parameters and no unreduced or irregular expressions anywhere in the map data.
